w1.text: Why: reading comes before writing. Mapping code → picture builds a mental renderer. Every distractor is a real misconception (mixing up justify-content and align-items). Options are drawn with real CSS, so they can never lie.

w2.text: Why: a fast warm-up for vocabulary. The right column is visual, so learners link property → effect rather than word → word. It checks on every tap, so the rhythm stays quick and low-stakes.

w3.text: Why: two choices, one concept — the cascade. The trap ("the later rule wins") is the most common specificity mistake. The reveal shows the scores, so the rule sticks, not just the answer.

w4.text: Why: Duolingo's word bank, adapted to syntax. Recall with guardrails — no typos to punish. The live preview renders wrong picks too, so 'flex + center' shows why it only centers one way.

w5.text: Why: CSS is visual, so train the eye. Direct manipulation with instant feedback, like nudging a value in DevTools. The dashed ghost target makes 'close but not quite' visible.

w6.text: Why: most real CSS time is debugging, and CSS fails silently — no errors. Expected-vs-actual mirrors how developers actually spot bugs, and tapping a line is easy on a phone.

w7.text: Why: the hardest step — free recall with no options. Use it late in a lesson, after recognition. The live preview rewards partial progress and makes a misspelling visibly fail.

p1.text: Press Play to run the app. LEARN tab: 5 lessons (How CSS works, Box model, Flexbox, Grid, Common properties), 19 cards, each with a live playground — tap values and watch the demo and code update. The last card jumps to topic practice. PRACTICE tab: Mixed review or one question type. 5 hearts; misses come back at the end. +10 XP first try, +5 on retry.
